newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales up 6.9 pct yr/yr in August-BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales up 6.9 pct yr/yr in August-BRC.

text.p: UK "like-for-like" retail sales rose 6.9 percent in value in the year to August, continuing the run of healthy figures recorded over the summer, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) said.
This represented a bounce-back from the more moderate growth of 5.4 percent seen in July, giving an average increase of 6.5 percent in the June to August period.
"The underlying rate of increase in retail sales may now be stabilising at an annual rate of 6.0 to 6.5 percent," the BRC said.
Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC economic affairs committee, said retailers enjoyed a strong performance in August.
"Sentiment in the industry is improving as consumer confidence strengthens and the housing market picks up," he said.
The BRC's chief economic adviser, Andrew Sentance, said the improvement in consumer spending was supported by other indicators, including a stronger housing market and rising consumer credit.

"In the current climate of low interest rates, retail sales should continue to grow at the present rate -- providing a welcome lift to UK economic growth in the second half of this year and in 1997," he said.
